title: Make It Tiny
pin_title: ADHD Start: Make the First Step So Small It Feels Silly
description: ADHD brains often treat starting as the hardest part. Make the first action so small it feels almost silly: open the document, write one sentence, put on shoes. Once the tiny step is done, the next one is easier because momentum exists. The goal is not the whole task. The goal is the first visible move. #ADHD #Starting #ADHDTips #Focus

title: Someone Nearby
pin_title: ADHD Focus: Use a Quiet Body Double
description: Working alone can feel heavier with ADHD. A quiet body double — someone in the same room or on a call who is simply present — often makes starting and staying easier. No talking required. The presence reduces the friction of being alone with the task. Try it for one block and notice the difference. #ADHD #BodyDouble #ADHDTips #Focus

title: Kind Timer
pin_title: ADHD Timer: Use One That Never Shouts
description: A harsh timer can trigger avoidance. Choose a timer that ends softly — a gentle chime or a visual fade — and set it shorter than you think you need. The kindness of the signal makes returning feel possible instead of punishing. Short gentle sessions build trust with your brain. #ADHD #Timer #ADHDTips #Focus

title: One Thing Visible
pin_title: ADHD Screen: Keep Only One Task in Sight
description: Multiple open tabs and lists create noise that freezes action. Close everything except the single next step. When the brain sees only one thing, starting becomes lighter. Pair it with permission to stop when the timer ends. Clarity reduces friction more than motivation does. #ADHD #Focus #ADHDTips #OneThing

title: Return Gently
pin_title: ADHD Restart: Come Back Without the Guilt Speech
description: Gaps happen with ADHD. The gap is not a moral failure. Write the next tiny step on a note, then start from there instead of replaying the whole story of what was missed. A gentle return saves more energy than a perfect restart. Future you will thank present you for the soft landing. #ADHD #SelfCompassion #ADHDTips #Restart
